FINDINGS. Two, both NON-BLOCKING, both new relative to the reviewer-A record already on this branch (which I read after taking my own measurements, to avoid duplicating it; my numbers are independent).

F1 (NON-BLOCKING, REPRODUCED). An UNREADABLE proof record is silent in both rules, and lwb_proof_integrity's docstring justifies that silence with a claim that is not true. Reproduction, through the shipped hook: with proof/master.json containing '{{{ not json at all' on branch 'master' and a publish command, the hook emitted NO lwb_proof_required finding (collect_proof_ids_ex matches on FILENAME only, so the corrupt file counts as a record that exists) and NO lwb_proof_integrity finding (collect_matched_proof_facts returns (None, None) on a JSONDecodeError, and the rule treats None as no-opinion). Net: a proof record that could not be parsed is indistinguishable from a valid one that has nothing wrong with it -- the exact "I could not check must never share a representation with I checked and found nothing" shape HANDOFF.md item 5 names as this project's standing defect pattern. lwb_proof_integrity's module docstring says "A missing or unreadable record is lwb_proof_required's territory, not this rule's"; I measured that lwb_proof_required does not cover the unreadable case at all, because it never reads content. Why I am NOT charging it as blocking: (i) the filename-only matching in lwb_proof_required is PRE-EXISTING on main, not introduced here -- this PR fails to close it and mis-describes it, it does not create it; (ii) both rules ship at "warn" with nothing armed to deny, so the cost is a missed warning, never a false deny; (iii) inside THIS repository scripts/lwb_check_proof.py is the authoritative backstop and does reject a corrupt record (measured, P3). The fix is small and local -- have collect_matched_proof_facts distinguish "no such file" from "file present but unparseable" and let the rule say so -- and the docstring sentence should be corrected either way, since it currently tells a reader another rule covers something no rule covers.

F2 (NON-BLOCKING, ACCURACY). lwb_proof_coverage's parity claim with CI is one match short, in the false-positive direction. collect_landed_unproven's docstring says 'A "matching record" means the same two things check_coverage accepts', and the module docstring says the scan "under-matches on purpose -- a merge this scan cannot see is a missed warning, not a false one". scripts/lwb_check_proof.py::check_coverage accepts THREE things: the record's content "pr", the exempt list, and `any(len(c) >= 7 and sha.startswith(c) for c in proved_commits)` -- the record's own "commit" field. The adapter implements the first two (plus filename-derived ids, which CI does not use and which only widens coverage, a safe direction) but not the "commit" match. proof/schema.json makes "commit" REQUIRED and "pr" OPTIONAL, so a consuming repo may legitimately write records with only "commit"; a reachable commit whose subject ends "(#N)" would then be warned about by the hook while CI considers it proven -- a false positive, the one direction the docstring promises does not happen. Latent in THIS repository: I checked all 22 records and every one carries an integer "pr", and CI's commit-match is itself near-dead for squash merges (a record written inside a PR cannot name the squash sha, as that script's own comment says). Non-blocking for that reason; worth either implementing the third match or correcting the two docstrings.
